BORGHINI · MERIDA eSPRESSO 400 S EQ · SHIMANO STEPS E6100 · EW-EN100 · ESP32-S3

Borghini's dashboard

A handlebar touchscreen that reads live ride data from a Shimano STEPS e-bike over Bluetooth, with no wires to the bike. It also does a GPS track, heart rate, an iPhone music remote, internet radio and MP3s.

Bike sideShimano EW-EN100
Screen2.8" 240×320 touch

Why Bluetooth? Shimano's EW-EN100 wireless unit already sends the bike's live data over Bluetooth LE: speed, assist mode, battery, range, trip and lights. We decoded it, so the dashboard just listens. There's no cable to splice, no custom circuit board, and nothing to break on the bike.

Built for Borghini, a blue Merida eSpresso 400 S EQ. It's named after Lamborghini, because blue is 蓝 lán (lam in Cantonese).

Read-only by design

The ESP32 only subscribes to notifications. It never writes to the bike, so it can't change assist, settings, firmware or the 25 km/h limit. If it crashes, the bike rides exactly as normal.

Hobby project, not affiliated with or endorsed by Shimano. The protocol notes come from captures of one bike (EN100 firmware 4.6.0.0). Other units and firmware may differ.

Chapter 02What it does

Live

Ride data

Speed, assist mode (OFF / ECO / NORMAL / HIGH), battery, range for the current mode, trip and lights, from the EW-EN100. Cadence and max/average speed are decoded too.

Live

Heart rate

From any Bluetooth heart-rate sender: a chest strap, a watch broadcasting HR, or an Apple Watch through the HeartCast app.

Live

iPhone music remote

Pairs as E-TUBE Tap. Shows what's playing in Spotify or Music and controls play, skip and volume (Apple Media Service).

Live

Internet radio

Nine built-in stations over Wi-Fi (Hong Kong, Beijing, Singapore, Australia, UK), through the board's speaker, with a volume boost.

Live

MP3 player

Every .mp3 on the microSD card, with shuffle and repeat.

Needs GPS

Map trail

Draws the line you've ridden, with a scale bar. The code is ready. It runs a simulated route until a GPS module is fitted (Phase 9).

Chapter 03How it works

The ESP32-S3 plays two Bluetooth roles at once. As a central, it connects out to the bike and to a heart-rate sender. As a peripheral, it lets your iPhone connect in for music. One shared scan finds both the bike and the heart-rate sender.

The one rule: the EN100 talks to one device at a time

When Shimano Ride on your phone is connected to the EN100, the EN100 stops advertising and the dashboard can't see it. Ride reconnects quietly in the background, so force-quit Shimano Ride when you ride with the dashboard. The iPhone's own link to the dashboard (for music) is separate and stays connected.

Chapter 05Build, step by step

Each phase ends with a gate, a check that must pass before you move on. Tick the boxes as you go. Your progress stays in this browser.

Set up the Arduino IDE

Everything here works in the free Arduino IDE 2. No command line needed.

  1. Install Arduino IDE 2 from arduino.cc/en/software.
  2. Add the ESP32 boards: File → Preferences (macOS: Arduino IDE → Settings). Under Additional boards manager URLs, paste:
    https://espressif.github.io/arduino-esp32/package_esp32_index.json
  3. Tools → Board → Boards Manager, search esp32, and install esp32 by Espressif Systems (3.3.x).
  4. Tools → Manage Libraries, and install each of these:

lvgllvgl by kisvegabor9.2.2, 9.6.0

ESP32-audioI2SESP32-audioI2S-master by schreibfaul13.4.7, 4.0.1

  1. Get the code: on the GitHub page, click Code → Download ZIP and unzip it (or git clone it).
  2. Copy firmware/arduino_libraries/lv_conf.h into your Arduino libraries folder, next to the lvgl folder. That's Documents/Arduino/libraries/ on macOS and Windows. LVGL won't build without it.

2
phone · 2 min

Free the EN100

While anything is connected to the EN100, it doesn't advertise at all. Force-quit Shimano Ride and E-TUBE Project (swipe them away in the app switcher), or turn Bluetooth off in Settings. Control Centre's toggle only disconnects accessories. Check for iPads, Macs and Garmins nearby that might connect too.

3
bench · 10 min

Find the EN100

  1. File → Open → firmware/ble_explorer/ble_explorer.ino. Use the board settings from Phase 1.
  2. Plug the board in with a USB-C data cable and pick it under Tools → Port.
  3. Click Upload (→). Wait for Hard resetting via RTS pin.
  4. Open Tools → Serial Monitor and set it to 115200 baud, Newline.
  5. Then press the board's RST button. The scan prints in the first 10 seconds, so if the monitor wasn't open you miss it. Type s and press Enter to scan again.

Scan once with the bike off and once with it on. The device that only appears with the bike on is your EN100. It advertises under the bike's name (set in E-TUBE) with the Shimano service:

[13] c4:82:cf:xx:xx:xx  RSSI  -70  name='Borghini'   <== Shimano?
       svc 000018ff-5348-494d-414e-4f5f424c4500
       svc 000018ef-5348-494d-414e-4f5f424c4500

Every Shimano UUID ends in the ASCII bytes SHIMANO_BLE.

5
bike on a stand · 15 min

Check the fields on your bike

Your bike or firmware may differ, so confirm the byte map before you trust it. tools/en100_capture.py resets the board, waits for the EN100, connects and logs everything. Start it, then switch the bike on:

pip3 install pyserial
python3 tools/en100_capture.py 110 > capture.txt
  1. Wait 15 s without touching anything (baseline).
  2. Press assist up one step every 5 s. Type 02 byte 1 should step 0 → 1 → 2 → 3.
  3. Turn the light on, then off. Type 01 byte 6 should go 2, then 1.
  4. Lift the rear wheel and turn the pedals, slow then faster. Type 02 bytes 2–3 (speed) and byte 5 (cadence) should rise.
  5. Compare the range in type 03 with the display, or with Shimano Ride later.
6
bench · 20 min

Flash the dashboard

  1. In the firmware/etube_ui folder, copy secrets.example.h to a new file named secrets.h (it's git-ignored, so your details stay private).
  2. File → Open → firmware/etube_ui/etube_ui.ino. The IDE opens every file in the folder as a tab. In the secrets.h tab, fill in WIFI_SSID, WIFI_PASS and, optionally, BIKE_ADDR: your EN100's address as the explorer printed it, so the dashboard ignores other riders' bikes.
  3. Check Tools → Partition Scheme → Custom (it won't fit otherwise), then click Upload. The first build takes a few minutes, mostly the Chinese font.
  4. Open the Serial Monitor at 115200 to watch the log.

Command line:

cd firmware/etube_ui
cp secrets.example.h secrets.h      # then edit it
arduino-cli upload --fqbn esp32:esp32:esp32s3:CDCOnBoot=cdc,FlashSize=16M,PartitionScheme=custom,PSRAM=opi -p /dev/cu.usbmodem101 .

Press RST, then switch the bike off and on. The serial log shows the link:

Bike: found 'Borghini' (c4:82:cf:xx:xx:xx) RSSI -66
Bike: connecting...
Bike: live data
7
phone · 5 min

Pair the iPhone

On the iPhone: Settings → Bluetooth → E-TUBE Tap, then accept the pairing. The MUSIC tab shows what's playing. For heart rate, run HeartCast on the iPhone with an Apple Watch, or wear any Bluetooth chest strap. The dashboard finds it by itself.

8
weekend

Power, case and mount

Battery: look for a small 2-pin battery connector on the board. If there is one, a 1S LiPo charges through the board's USB-C. Check the plug polarity first. Cheap LiPo leads are often wired backwards. Without a connector, use a slim USB power bank. Screen, Bluetooth and Wi-Fi draw roughly 150–300 mA, so 2000 mAh lasts about 6–10 h.

Case: to start, a waterproof phone bag on the handlebar works. The touchscreen works through the clear film. For the final build, print the case: ready-made STLs for the ES3C28P, sized from the manufacturer's drawing. It holds a 103450 LiPo, the speaker and a power switch, has a USB-C opening for charging, and clicks into a Garmin quarter-turn mount. 68.8 × 104.8 × 28.4 mm. The print sheet lists materials (PETG/ASA + a TPU gasket), screws and assembly. No printer? Send the files to a friend, a makerspace, or an online service. It hasn't been test-printed yet, so print the 10-minute Garmin fit test and the bezel first.

9
optional · 30 min

Add GPS for a real map

The map code reads standard NMEA at 9600 baud on GPIO14 and switches from the simulated route to the real one as soon as data arrives. Wire module TX → GPIO14, RX → GPIO21 (optional), VCC → 3V3, GND → GND. Check that both pins are broken out on your board's headers. If not, change the two numbers in gps_track.cpp. Go outside: the first fix takes 30 s to a few minutes.

Chapter 06The Shimano data

Everything comes from one characteristic: 2ac1 in service 000018ef-5348-494d-414e-4f5f424c4500. It sends a notification about every 250 ms. Byte 0 is the message type, and the types take turns, so each one repeats about once a second. Numbers are little-endian, and byte positions count from 0. Battery comes from the standard Battery service.

Type 02: riding

ByteFieldScaleStatus
1Assist mode0 OFF · 1 ECO · 2 NORMAL · 3 HIGHConfirmed
2–3Speed0.1 km/hConfirmed
4?0–3 while pedallingUnknown
5CadencerpmLikely
6? flagwent to 1 at ~26 km/hUnknown

Type 03: distance, speed, range

ByteFieldScaleStatus
1–4Trip distancemLikely
5–6Second distance counter (not the odometer)mUnknown
7Battery%Likely
9–10Average speed0.1 km/hLikely
11–12Maximum speed0.1 km/hLikely
13–14 · 15–16 · 17–18Range in HIGH · NORMAL · ECOkmECO confirmed

Type 01: status · Battery service

WhereFieldScaleStatus
01 byte 6Light2 on · 1 offConfirmed
180f / 2a19Battery%Confirmed
types 00, 04Constant / rare; maybe Di2 gear fields this bike doesn't haveUnknown

The decoder

This is the heart of bike_ble.cpp. It runs on every notification and fills the same RideState the screens already draw from.

static void onData(NimBLERemoteCharacteristic *, uint8_t *d, size_t n, bool) {
  switch (d[0]) {
    case 0x02:                                    // riding
      ride.assist   = d[1] == 1 ? ASSIST_ECO : d[1] == 2 ? ASSIST_NORMAL
                    : d[1] == 3 ? ASSIST_HIGH : ASSIST_OFF;
      ride.speedKph = u16(d + 2) / 10.0f;
      ride.cadenceRpm = d[5];
      break;
    case 0x03:                                    // distance, speed, range
      ride.tripKm = u32(d + 1) / 1000.0f;
      ride.maxKph = u16(d + 11) / 10.0f;
      range[ASSIST_HIGH] = u16(d + 13);
      range[ASSIST_NORMAL] = u16(d + 15);
      range[ASSIST_ECO] = u16(d + 17);
      break;
    case 0x01:                                    // status
      ride.lightOn = d[6] == 2;
      break;
  }
  lastFrameMs = millis();                         // older than 3 s = NO BUS
}
Check every guess

Our first guess at the odometer was type 03 bytes 5–8 read as one number: 6,573 km. The bike has done about 3,000 km. Byte 7 turned out to be battery %, and bytes 5–6 something else. A value that looks plausible isn't confirmed until it matches the bike.

The full GATT table (both Shimano services, all 20 characteristics), example frames and the open questions are in the protocol notes. The raw captures are in captures/en100.

Chapter 07The dashboard

Five screens: change with the tab bar, or swipe. The status bar always says where the ride data comes from.

Status barMeaningWhat the screen does
BUS OKFrames from the EN100 in the last 3 sLive values. The assist buttons follow the bike.
NO BUSThe link dropped (bike off, out of range, phone took it)Speed shows 0. It never falls back to fake values.
SIM DATANo bike since power-onSimulated values, for testing the screens on the bench.
ScreenShows
RIDESpeed, assist mode, battery, range for the current mode (-- km with assist OFF), trip, LIGHT ON/OFF, heart rate, mini player
MAPBreadcrumb track (up to 1,500 points, one every 5 m), scale bar, speed, heart rate, ride time
MUSICiPhone now-playing: title, artist, app, progress, play/skip/volume
RADIONine stations; volume 0–21, then BOOST up to +12 dB
MP3Library from microSD (up to 400 files, 3 folders deep), shuffle, repeat
The assist buttons only follow the bike

The link is read-only, so tapping ECO / NORMAL / HIGH while live does nothing. Change mode with the bike's own switch. Pressing the switch electronically is a separate add-on idea: see controlling assist and lights.

Serial commands at 115200: p screenshot, t120,248 fake tap, r6 play station 6, s stop audio, c clock. tools/screenshot.py uses them to save PNGs straight from the frame buffer.

Chapter 08Phone + dashboard

LinkWho connectsCan run together?
Dashboard ↔ EN100Dashboard connects outNo The EN100 takes one link. Whoever connects first wins.
Shimano Ride ↔ EN100Phone connects out
iPhone ↔ dashboard (“E-TUBE Tap”)Phone connects inYes Music and bike data, alongside the EN100 link
Heart-rate sender ↔ dashboardDashboard connects outYes
  1. Riding with the dashboard: force-quit Shimano Ride, then switch the bike on. Keep Bluetooth on for music.
  2. Need Ride (odometer, settings, firmware)? Open it. The dashboard shows NO BUS while Ride holds the bike.
  3. Back to the dashboard: force-quit Ride, then switch the bike off and on.

Chapter 09Troubleshooting

Everything here happened during the first build session.

SymptomCauseFix
EN100 missing from scansShimano Ride is connected (maybe in the background), or the bike is offForce-quit Ride, switch the bike off and on. Diff a bike-off and a bike-on scan.
Connects once, never againConnecting while a scan is running. NimBLE refusesStop the scan before connect(). Fixed in bike_ble.cpp.
“Sketch too big” / “text section exceeds available space”Partition Scheme isn't CustomTools → Partition Scheme → Custom. The dashboard is 3.6 MB.
lv_conf.h: No such file, or odd LVGL errorslv_conf.h not next to the lvgl libraryCopy firmware/arduino_libraries/lv_conf.h into Documents/Arduino/libraries/.
secrets.h: No such fileThe template wasn't copiedCopy secrets.example.h to secrets.h in the sketch folder.
No port in Tools → PortCharge-only USB cable, or the board isn't in a mode the computer seesUse a data cable. Still nothing: hold BOOT, tap RST, release BOOT, upload, then press RST.
Serial monitor blank after uploadThe scan printed before the monitor openedOpen the monitor first, then press RST, or type s. Also check USB CDC On Boot: Enabled.
Upload: “No serial data received”, port still listedThe S3's native USB serial locked up after many fast resetsUnplug the board and plug it back in.
Can't open the portArduino IDE's Serial Monitor holds itClose the monitor tab.
invalid conversion from 'int' to 'lv_part_t'LVGL 9.6 is stricter than 9.2Use LV_PART_MAIN instead of 0 (fixed in the repo).
MP3 tab: “no card”Card not seated, or not FAT32/exFATRe-seat or reformat the card. Watch the serial log for SD: lines.
Disconnect reason 520Supervision timeout: the bike was switched offNormal. The dashboard rescans by itself.

Chapter 11Safety

  • Read-only. The firmware reads and subscribes. It never writes a characteristic value and never touches Shimano's settings service (18ff). Writing to unknown characteristics on a motor controller is a bad idea.
  • 25 km/h. Nothing here changes the assist limit. It's a legal limit for pedelecs in Australia and the EU.
  • Eyes on the road. Glance at the screen; don't use it while riding in traffic. Mount it firmly, where it can't swing into the bars.
  • LiPo cells. Check the polarity, don't crush or puncture them, and don't charge one that's swollen or hot.
  • Warranty. Nothing plugs into the bike, but treat this as an extra display, not a replacement for the bike's own unit.
